newsitem.title: UK: UK oil exlorers gain after Clyde bid.
newsitem.headline: UK oil exlorers gain after Clyde bid.

text.p: Shares in UK oil exploration companies rose in early trading on Wednesday after Gulf Canada made a 432 million stg bid for Clyde Petroleum.

Enterprise Oil Plc was up 3-1/2p at 575 by 0822 GMT, Cairn Energy Plc was up 14p at 404, Hardy Oil & Gas Plc was up 10-1/2p at 283-1/2 and British Borneo Plc was up 7-1/2p at 664. Clyde was up 27p at 111-1/2.

Analysts said the bid could be a prelude to more takeover activity in the sector, and as Clyde shares rose 30-1/2p to 115 by 0849 GMT -- well ahead of the bid level -- they said it could attract a higher offer.
"Clyde is definitely a very attractive company that has been grotesquely undervalued in the market in terms of price to cash flow," said Jurjen Lunshoff, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing.

"My feeling is that 105p is too cheap, it seems to undervalue the company's assets and I think the market is telling us that too...it seems a pretty opportunistic bid, Clyde has rapidly rising production coming through and the cash generation of the company is excellent."

Lunshoff said it was no surprise to see shares rising across the sector. "Companies have been dramatically undervalued by a number of institutions and there is nothing like a bid to wake people up," he said.

Wendy Anderson, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said the bid could prompt more sustained share gains across the sector. "It keeps the focus on the e&p (exploration and production) sector and raises the question of whether it deserves a re-rating," she said.
Clyde said it would issue a response to the bid approach in due course.
